claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I have one child that I'd like to check eligibility for. His name is Alex and he's 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have a good starting point. Let me gather a bit more detail about Alex to assess eligibility properly.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your living situation a bit better.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's important information. Let me ask a follow-up question about your circumstances:

**Do you work in the UK, or do you have any UK income?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't work in the UK and I don't have any UK income.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Before I can provide you with a final decision, I need to check the specific eligibility criteria. Let me review the official government guidance on Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the guidance I've just reviewed, I can see there's a specific section about living abroad. Let me ask one more clarifying question:

**Are you a Crown servant (such as working for the British Armed Forces or diplomatic service abroad)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant. I'm not working for the British Armed Forces or diplomatic service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Based on the information you've provided and the official eligibility criteria I've reviewed, I can now provide you with my assessment.

According to the UK government's Child Benefit eligibility rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and **you live in the UK**. 

The guidance also states that you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant - but since you've confirmed you're not a Crown servant and you're living abroad without a UK income, the standard eligibility requirement of living in the UK is not met.

Additionally, since you don't have UK income and are living abroad, you would not meet the alternative eligibility criteria for those living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

The reason is that the main eligibility requirement for Child Benefit is that you must live in the UK. Since you're currently living abroad without UK income and are not a Crown servant, you don't meet the eligibility criteria that would allow people living abroad to claim Child Benefit.

If your circumstances change in the future - such as if you move back to the UK or become a Crown servant - your eligibility status may change. If you have any other questions about this decision or your circumstances change, feel free to contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
